root_cause_label: Incorrect interpolation order: ffill/bfill applied before interpolate, eliminating NaNs and preventing linear interpolation of interior gaps
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent wrote a fill_missing_values function that applies ffill and bfill before interpolate, causing interior NaNs to be step-filled instead of linearly interpolated, producing wrong water-level values and incorrect flood event counts, and never detected this numerical error during verification.
t_err_evidence: Step 4: The agent writes fill_missing_values with the sequence df.ffill() -> df.bfill() -> df.interpolate(). Applying ffill/bfill first eliminates all NaN values before interpolate runs, so interpolate finds nothing to do for interior gaps and the gap at row 5 (between 3.2 and 3.7) is step-filled to 3.2 instead of being linearly interpolated to ~3.45.
t_commit_evidence: Step 9: The updated script runs successfully (returncode 0) and overwrites all three station CSV files and writes /app/flood_summary.json with incorrect flood event counts derived from the wrongly interpolated data. After this point the source data is corrupted and the JSON output is locked in.
trigger_explanation: The agent's stated plan was correct (interpolate interior gaps linearly, fill boundaries with first/last available values) but the code generation placed ffill and bfill before interpolate rather than after, implementing step-fill semantics for interior gaps instead of the required linear interpolation.
